name: Technology strategy and advisory
card: A costed plan for what to build, buy and retire, in an order your leadership can approve.
title: A technology plan your leadership can sign.
meta: Technology strategy and advisory for growing businesses: roadmaps, build or buy decisions, vendor selection and fractional CTO support. Shiro Labs, Jakarta.
lede: We turn a pile of tools, requests and opinions into one plan: what to build, what to buy, what to retire, what it costs and in what order. Available as a fixed project or as ongoing fractional CTO support.
facts: 2 to 6 weeks, or a monthly retainer
The roadmap, cost model and decision log
helps: Every team has bought its own tools
Spend creeps up, data ends up in five places and nobody can say what is actually used.
Big decisions rest on one person's opinion
Build or buy, which vendor, which platform. A short written comparison beats a long argument.
Engineering and the business want different things
A roadmap in plain language lets both sides trade off cost, risk and speed using the same facts.
There is no technical leader on the team
Many companies need a CTO's judgement a few days a month, not a full-time hire.
does: Technology review
What you run today, who uses it, what it costs and where it is fragile, written down on a page.
Roadmap and budget
A costed plan in quarters, with owners, dependencies and the effect of each item.
Build or buy decisions
Options compared on cost, risk, lock-in and fit, with a recommendation and the reasoning.
Vendor and tool selection
Requirements, a shortlist, demos and a scored comparison, so the choice can be explained later.
Fractional CTO
A few days a month of senior judgement: reviews, hiring input and a second opinion on big calls.
Hiring and team design
Role definitions, interview questions and a view on what to hire for and what to contract.
runs: Listen
Interviews with the people who use and run the systems, plus a read of contracts, bills and incidents.
Map
One page showing systems, owners, costs and risks, checked with you.
Decide
Options and a recommendation, discussed in a working session rather than mailed as a report.
Follow up
A check-in after a quarter to see what shipped and to adjust the plan.
faq: Do you only advise, or also build?
Both. Some clients take the plan and run with it, others ask us to deliver parts of it. The plan stands either way.
Is a retainer required?
No. Most start with a fixed-scope project. A retainer makes sense once there is a roadmap to steer.
Do you take vendor commissions?
No. You are the only one paying us, which is why the comparisons can be blunt.

name: Custom software and web apps
card: Internal tools, customer portals and web products, built in small steps and easy for your team to run.
title: Software built around how your business actually works.
meta: Custom software and web apps for businesses: internal tools, customer portals, dashboards and MVPs, built fast and kept maintainable. Shiro Labs, Jakarta.
lede: When a spreadsheet, an off-the-shelf tool or a chain of manual steps stops being enough, we build the software that fits: fast, accessible, and simple enough for your team to keep running.
facts: 6 to 12 weeks for a first release
The code, the infrastructure and the docs
helps: The business runs on spreadsheets
They work until two people edit at once, a formula breaks or the one person who understands them leaves.
Off-the-shelf tools almost fit
You pay for features you do not use and still work around the ones you need.
An idea needs proving before a big spend
A small, working first version teaches more than a long specification.
The old internal system is slow and feared
Nobody dares change it, so it only gets slower and harder to use.
does: Internal tools and portals
Dashboards, approval flows and admin screens that replace spreadsheets and email threads.
Customer-facing web apps
Booking, ordering, account and self-service pages that stay fast on a mid-range phone.
MVPs and prototypes
A narrow, working first release to test the idea with real users before more is spent.
Design systems
A small set of consistent components, so new screens are quick to build and look like one product.
Accessibility and performance
Keyboard, screen reader and speed checks built in from the start, not added at the end.
Modernizing legacy tools
Replace a feared old system in slices, without a risky big-bang switch.
runs: Understand
We watch people do the work and write down the five tasks that matter most.
Prototype
Clickable screens in days, so the shape is argued over before code exists.
Build
Weekly releases to a real environment. You see progress as working software.
Hand over
Documentation, a walkthrough and the option of ongoing support.
faq: Who owns the code?
You do. The repository sits in your account from the first day.
Can you work with our existing developers?
Yes. We pair with them and follow your conventions, or set up simple ones if there are none.
What about maintenance after launch?
We offer a small monthly support plan, or hand over fully. Either way nothing is locked to us.

name: Systems integration and automation
card: Connect your ERP, CRM, store and finance tools so data moves by itself and nobody re-keys it.
title: Your systems, talking to each other.
meta: Systems integration and automation: connect ERP, CRM, e-commerce and finance tools, automate repeated work and build reliable reporting. Shiro Labs, Jakarta.
lede: Most businesses run on several tools that do not agree with each other. We connect them, automate the repeated steps and make exceptions visible, so people spend their time on decisions instead of copying data.
facts: Integration code, runbooks, a data map
helps: The same data is typed in twice
Orders, customers and invoices copied between tools by hand. Slow, and every copy is a chance for a mistake.
Month-end takes a week
Finance spends days finding where two systems disagree instead of analyzing the numbers.
Reports come from someone's spreadsheet
The numbers depend on a manual export that only one person knows how to run.
A new tool arrived and nothing connects to it
Every added system makes the data harder to trust unless it is wired in on purpose.
does: Data and process mapping
A diagram of how information really flows today, and which system owns each record.
ERP, CRM and finance integration
Reliable connections between the tools you already pay for, using their APIs and webhooks.
Workflow automation
Approvals, notifications and routine tasks that run on their own, with a person handling exceptions.
Data pipelines and reporting
One trusted place for the numbers, with dashboards that refresh without anyone exporting a file.
Error handling and monitoring
Retries, logs and a daily list of anything that failed, so nothing breaks silently.
Migration and clean-up
Move data between systems with checks, and fix duplicates and gaps on the way.
runs: Map
We trace one record, such as an order, through every system and note where it is copied.
Choose
One source of truth per record, and the simplest integration that keeps it that way.
Connect
Built in slices, each one running on real data before the next starts.
Watch
Alerts and a daily exceptions list, then a review after the first month-end.
faq: Do you work with our ERP?
Probably. If it has an API or a database we can reach, we can connect it. We check this in the first week.
Low-code or custom code?
Low-code for simple, low-risk flows and custom code where reliability or volume matters. We explain the trade-off.
What happens when a sync fails?
It retries, then lands on an exceptions list that a person reviews. Nothing fails silently.

name: Cloud, DevOps and reliability
card: Hosting, pipelines and monitoring that cost less, fail less and let you ship on any weekday.
title: Infrastructure that stays up and stays affordable.
meta: Cloud, DevOps and reliability: cloud setup and migration, CI/CD pipelines, monitoring, backups and cost control. Shiro Labs, Jakarta.
lede: We set up and tidy the hosting, pipelines and monitoring behind your product, so releases are routine, outages are noticed in minutes and the cloud bill makes sense.
facts: Teams on AWS, GCP, Azure or a VPS
helps: Releases are a nervous event
A checklist, a Friday freeze and one person who knows the steps. We turn the ritual into a pipeline.
Customers find outages before you do
Without checks and alerts, the first report of a problem comes from the person it hurt.
The cloud bill keeps growing
Oversized servers, forgotten resources and no tagging. Most bills have easy savings hiding in them.
The setup lives in someone's head
Servers configured by hand are hard to repeat and harder to recover.
does: Cloud setup and migration
A sensible account structure, separate environments and a migration plan with a rollback.
CI/CD pipelines
Fast builds, selective test runs and one-step deploys and rollbacks.
Infrastructure as code
Your setup written down as code, so it can be reviewed, repeated and recovered.
Monitoring and alerting
Checks on what customers feel, alerts that page the right person and a public status page.
Backups and recovery
Backups that are tested by restoring them, and a written plan for the bad day.
Cost review
Where the money goes, what to turn off or resize, and alerts before the bill surprises you.
runs: Inventory
We list what runs, what it costs and how it is deployed today. No changes yet.
Stabilize
Fix the riskiest gaps first: backups, alerts and the manual release steps.
Automate
Pipelines and infrastructure code replace the manual steps, one at a time.
Hand over
Runbooks, dashboards and a walkthrough for whoever is on call.
faq: Which cloud do you work with?
Mostly AWS, and comfortable on GCP, Azure or plain VPS hosting. We recommend what fits your size, not what is fashionable.
Do you provide on-call?
Not by default. We set things up so your team can be on call, and can discuss a support plan separately.
Will a migration cause downtime?
We plan migrations with a rehearsal and a rollback and aim for no visible downtime, though some cutovers need a short window.

name: AI adoption and automation
card: Find where AI saves real time in your business, build it with a person in the loop and measure the result.
title: AI where it pays for itself, and nowhere else.
meta: AI adoption and automation: pick the right use cases, build assistants and agents with human review, and measure results. Shiro Labs, Jakarta.
lede: Most AI projects fail on the choice of problem or on trust, not on technology. We help you pick the few tasks where AI will save time, build them with review steps and measure whether they work.
facts: Teams with a repeated, text-heavy task
helps: Everyone wants AI and nobody knows where
A shortlist ranked by value, risk and effort beats a scattered set of experiments.
A chatbot pilot embarrassed the team
Systems that invent answers lose trust quickly. Guardrails and review keep them useful.
Staff already paste company data into chat tools
Without an approved way to use AI, people use their own, with your data.
Nobody can say if it works
Without a test set of real examples, every change is a guess.
does: Use-case discovery
We list candidate tasks and rank them by time saved, risk and how easy the output is to check.
Assistants with review
Drafting replies, summaries and reports, with a person approving anything that leaves the building.
Workflow and agent automation
Multi-step tasks such as triage, data entry and routing, with limits on what the agent may do.
Evaluation sets
Real examples with the right answers, so every prompt, model or change is scored.
Security and data policy
What data may go to which model, where it is stored and how misuse is caught.
Monitoring and cost
Quality and spend tracked after launch, with alerts when either drifts.
runs: Choose
One task with clear value and a way to check the output.
Pilot
A narrow version with a person approving, running on real work.
Measure
Accuracy, time saved and cost per task, reported plainly, including the failures.
Decide
Expand, adjust or stop, based on the numbers.
faq: Which models do you use?
We stay model-agnostic and choose on accuracy, cost and your data policy.
Is our data safe?
We agree a data policy before the pilot and use providers and settings that fit it. Sensitive data can stay in your own environment.
Do you build chatbots?
Sometimes, but we usually start with drafts and internal tools, where mistakes are cheap and a person checks the result.

name: Quality, security and audits
card: Independent checks on your software, delivery and security, with a ranked fix list and tests that keep it fixed.
title: An independent check, in writing.
meta: Quality, security and audits: technical due diligence, security and risk review, performance audits and test automation. Shiro Labs, Jakarta.
lede: A second pair of eyes on what you have built or are about to buy. We review code, delivery and security, rank the findings by effect and effort and, where useful, build the automated tests that keep problems from coming back.
facts: The report, the tests, the fix list
helps: An investor or buyer will look at the tech
A review before they do tells you what they will find, while there is still time to fix it.
Releases break things that worked
Without automated tests the same bugs return, and every release needs a manual pass.
Nobody has checked security in a while
Shared passwords, missing two-factor and untested backups are common and cheap to fix.
A vendor delivered something and you cannot tell how good it is
An independent review of the code and the delivery gives you facts before you accept it.
does: Technical due diligence
A written view of the code, architecture, team practices and risks, for investors, buyers or your own board.
Security and risk review
Access, secrets, dependencies, backups and data handling, checked against practical good practice.
Performance and reliability audit
Speed on real devices, failure points and behavior under load, with evidence.
Test automation
End-to-end and API suites that guard the paths that cost money when they break.
Release quality gates
The right checks on every change, blocking only on what matters.
Fix plan
Every finding ranked by effect and effort, with a short list your team can ship first.
runs: Scope
We agree what is reviewed, what is out of bounds and who sees the result.
Review
Code, configuration, pipelines and interviews, gathered into evidence.
Report
A written finding list ranked by effect and effort, walked through in a session.
Fix
Optional: we build the tests and fixes, or coach your team through them.
faq: Is this a formal security audit or certification?
No. It is a practical review against good practice. A certification needs an accredited auditor, and we can help you prepare for one.
Do you cover legal compliance, such as UU PDP?
We can flag technical gaps against data protection requirements. We are not a law firm, so legal sign-off is separate.
Can you review something another vendor built?
Yes, that is common. We review it on its merits and report to you.
